The local SDS leaders -- leaderships were completely autonomously and democratically elected in the field in local communities, municipalities, and the regional level. In party forums, President Karadzic insisted that decision were not made by out-voting but through finding compromises and solutions which would be supported by a great majority of the present people. One of the main issues the Republika Srpska government was facing concerned the large number of Serbian refugees from the territories under Muslim-Croatian control, their accommodation, medical treatment, and the wounded and the provisions for war hospitals and war orphans. When Alija Izetbegovic became president of BH after the first multi-party elections, some Serbs voiced reservation about him, because a long time before the war he published a document entitled the "Islamic Declaration." Soon after the elections, Muslims and Croats started out-voting the Serbs in the Assembly and in the government, and then in all the organs of local government on the ground. President Karadzic persistently tried to reach an agreement with the SDA, but they rejected it with cynicism and sometimes with arrogance. Izetbegovic and Zulfikarpasic agreed with President Karadzic and Milosevic that the then-BH with Serbia and Montenegro, which would be joined by Macedonia, were to constitute a form of federation. Nevertheless, before the official announcement of the agreement on television, Mr. Zulfikarpasic received a telegram fax in which the Muslims expressed their opposition to any agreement with the Serbs. It came from the SDA party. Zulfikarpasic denounced Izetbegovic for being directly responsible for war in refusing this agreement. The Muslims maintained the same behaviour during all subsequent attempts to reach an agreement during the war. They violated the Cutileiro Plan and all war truces to which President Karadzic agreed. They used tricks and intrigue and accused the Serbs for the incidents they were causing. As Supreme Commander of the VRS, President Karadzic clearly and publicly told the army, its soldiers and officers, and the whole Serbian people in Republika Srpska that all conventions applicable to the conduct of war must be respected. Before the formation of the VRS, the multi -- the military units of the Muslims and Croats were already formed and were involved in widespread episodes of violence against the Serbs. The position of President Karadzic about crimes against civilians was clear: Civilian are innocent and no form of force may be applied against them regardless of their ethnicity or religion. When he received information about incidents involving civilians, he condemned them, replaced the officers, and the direct perpetrators were processed. He even issued orders to save Muslim civilians when the conflict between Muslims and Croats broke out. On the order of President Karadzic, thousands of Croat refugees were saved when they crossed over to the Republika Srpska territory. In Republika Srpska they received water, food, medicine, and temporary accommodation, and then the VRS enabled them to cross over to their own desired destination. In the first few years of the war, the Muslims from Bileca and Trebinje were voluntarily in the VRS units, and those who did not want to lived undisturbed in their houses with their families. It was only after receiving secret memos and threats from Alija Izetbegovic that they were persuaded to leave immediately the VRS and the territory where they lived without any problems. On 15th of July, 1995, Professor Karadzic had a meeting with President Karadzic. On that occasion, the liquidation of prisoners in Srebrenica was never mentioned, and Professor Karadzic had the impression that President Karadzic inform -- was informed about the unlawful killings of prisoners of war from Srebrenica. And that is a short summary, and at that moment I will not have questions for Professor Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. Professor Karadzic, as you have noted, your evidence in chief in this case has been admitted in writing, that is, through your witness statement in lieu of your oral testimony, and you will now be cross-examined by the representative of the Office of the Prosecutor, but given the time, we'll continue tomorrow morning. I'd like to advise you not to discuss with anybody else about your testimony while you are giving testimony here.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Unless there is anything to be raised, the hearing is adjourned. We will continue tomorrow morning at 9.00.
